featured.name: Chagai and Taftan, Pakistan-Iran border (approx.)
featured.headline: Flat alluvial desert whose slope, relief and albedo match Oxia Planum almost exactly.
featured.description: A 30 by 30 km block of alluvial fans and a bright dry-lake playa on the Pakistan-Iran border, in the Chagai and Taftan area, at about 630 m elevation. At 200 m its slope and relief are the closest of any gated block to Oxia Planum, the ExoMars landing site, and its albedo matches Oxia's. Landsat 8/9 and Sentinel-2 both read it as bare ground. The place name is approximate: the block was found by statistics, so check it on a map before quoting it.

shortfalls: Air pressure 93 kPa vs about 0.6 kPa on Mars

Clay mineralogy not confirmed: Macrostrat resolves only 'siliciclastic' here and the Sentinel-2 clay index is about 1.03

featured.name: Gerze, Ngari, northern Tibet (approx.)
featured.headline: High Tibetan volcanic terrain with Jezero-like slopes, but a weaker, less stable match.

featured.name: Atacama Desert, Yungay (Chile)
featured.headline: Hyperarid desert whose oxidising soils are a classic analog for Mars surface chemistry.
featured.description: The hyperarid core of the Atacama, around Yungay, is one of the driest places on Earth. Its soils have extremely low organic content and microbial activity, and are used as an analog for Mars's oxidising, dry regolith. The match is about surface chemistry and aridity rather than terrain: Yungay is flat, so it does not match the steep ground at Gale.
shortfalls: Much warmer and thicker air than Mars
Terrain is flatter than most Mars landing-site windows

references.title: Navarro-Gonzalez et al. 2003, Mars-like soils in the Atacama Desert, Chile, and the dry limit of microbial life. Science

featured.description: The Rio Tinto in southwest Spain is an acidic, iron-rich river with sulfate minerals such as jarosite. It is used as an analog for the sulfate and hematite-bearing rocks that Opportunity found at Meridiani Planum. The match is about water chemistry and minerals, not terrain.
matches: Iron sulfates and oxides as at Meridiani
shortfalls: Biologically active; Mars is not known to be
Hillier than Meridiani's very flat plain

references.title: Fernandez-Remolar et al. 2005, The Rio Tinto Basin, Spain: mineralogy, sedimentary geobiology, and implications for interpretation of outcrop on Mars. Earth and Planetary Science Letters

featured.why: The Rio Tinto in southwest Spain is an acidic, iron-rich river with sulfate minerals such as jarosite. It is used as an analog for the sulfate and hematite-bearing rocks that Opportunity found at Meridiani Planum. The match is about water chemistry and minerals, not terrain. No terrain values were computed for this site.

provenance.processing: Moon cards: three 'new' blocks and three reserves from results/v3_final_table.csv (composite across 10 categories, stability over 1,000 random re-weightings, distance to 166 catalogued sites, Landsat 8/9 and Sentinel-2 surface check). Values are the block's own values from earth_cells.json. 'Known' Moon cards (Mauna Kea, Wright Valley) are validation analogs. Mars cards: nine computed finalists from results/mars_final_table.csv (composite over 8 categories against four Mars sites, stability over 1,000 random re-weightings, distance to 251 catalogued sites, Landsat 8/9 and Sentinel-2 surface check; Mars terrain is the 200 m HRSC+MOLA blend) plus three literature analogs (Atacama, Lake Salda, Rio Tinto). Place names are approximate; 'new' means at least 150 km from catalogued sites and nothing found in web searches only.
